blocks.content: A driver is responsible for ensuring the vehicle is in good condition before driving. A poorly maintained vehicle is dangerous and can lead to accidents.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The POWER acronym stands for Petrol/Fuel, Oil, Water, Electrics, and Rubber (Tyres).
Daily pre-drive checks help identify potential mechanical failures before taking the vehicle on public roads.
A Pollution Under Control (PUC) Certificate is mandatory for driving legally and ensuring roadworthiness.
Proper vehicle maintenance directly reduces road accidents, improves fuel efficiency, and lowers emissions.

blocks.content: W — Water — Check radiator coolant and windshield washer water

rows: Ensure mechanical safety and operational readiness before driving
Ensure vehicular emissions comply with prescribed environmental standards
Renewed every 6 to 12 months depending on vehicle category
Petrol, Oil level, Coolant/Water, Lights/Electrics, Tyre pressure/Rubber
Tailpipe emission levels (CO, HC, Smoke density)

blocks.content: E — Electrics — Check headlights, brake lights, indicators, horn
R — Rubber / Tyres — Check tyre pressure and tread depth

items: Questions frequently test the full form of POWER: Petrol, Oil, Water, Electrics, Rubber.
Note the PUC validity period: 1 year for new BS-VI compliant motor vehicles, and 6 months for older vehicles.
Driving without a valid PUC certificate attracts penalties under Section 190(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act.

cells: Brake fluid level, brake response, no unusual noise
Headlights, brake lights, indicators, reverse lights all working
Clean and properly adjusted (rear view + both side mirrors)

items: All vehicles must have a valid PUC (Pollution Under Control) certificate
New vehicle: PUC required after 1 year
PUC renewal: Every 6 months for old vehicles
Driving without valid PUC: Fine Rs.10,000
PUC tests measure exhaust emission levels
